contentHtml:
What Twinkeep is

The same shot saved four times — once from your camera, once from a text, twice from an export. Twinkeep finds duplicate photos, videos, and audio on your Mac, quarantines the byte-identical extras for you, and brings you only the judgment calls.

It is three tools in one native app: a duplicate media cleaner, File Rules that watch folders and file new arrivals automatically, and Maintain utilities for everyday housekeeping. Everything runs on your Mac. No account, no telemetry, no subscription — one purchase.

You only review what is actually in doubt

Byte-identical files are matched by content, and their extras go straight to Quarantine. A thousand of them take no more of your time than one. Review is kept for the genuine maybes — the same shot re-cropped, re-exported, or resaved — where only you can say which to keep.

When one does need your eye, Twinkeep puts both copies on screen at full size, side by side, with zoom and pan moving together down to 100% pixels and a strip between them calling out exactly what differs: dimensions, file size, format, camera, date. One key decides it.

Nothing disappears

Every removal goes to Quarantine first — never straight to delete. Restore anything, any time, back to exactly where it came from. Browse it as a list, icons, gallery, or filmstrip. Emptying it permanently is the one action Twinkeep will not do without asking.

What we fixed, and why

Version 1.1 is mostly the result of going back through the app and asking what it was quietly getting wrong. Some of it is uncomfortable to write down, so here it is plainly.

  • Junk Sweep could delete your crash reports. It listed the folder macOS writes crash and hang reports into as “safe to clean”, and pre-selected it — which meant a routine cleanup quietly destroyed the same reports the Stability tool reads. That folder is now permanently off limits, with a test that fails if anyone ever puts it back.
  • Three tools said “nothing found” when they meant “I cannot look”. On the App Store build, Downloads Dust, Disk Analysis and Stability showed empty results when macOS had not granted folder access — indistinguishable from a clean Mac. They now say access is needed and offer to ask for it.
  • Memory Relief overstated what it freed. Quitting is a request an app can decline; one with unsaved changes stays open. Twinkeep counted those as freed memory. It now waits to see what actually closed and reports only that.
  • File Rules started working before you asked it to. It now ships switched off. Nothing on your Mac moves until you turn it on.
  • Folder sizes ignored hidden files, so the amount Junk Sweep promised was less than it actually reclaimed. Totals now include them.
  • The background stability monitor rewrote its entire history every minute. Now it appends a line.

None of that is exciting. All of it is the difference between a utility you can trust with your files and one you cannot.

Duplicate cleaning

  • Exact duplicates — SHA-256 content hashing finds byte-identical files whatever they are named; extras are quarantined for you automatically, and you can switch that off
  • Similar photos — perceptual matching groups the same shot re-cropped, re-exported or resaved, and always waits for your decision
  • Photos, video, and audio in one scanner
  • Scan any folders you choose, including external drives
  • Smart keep policy — prefers Live Photo and HEIC originals over copy-like names, then the older file and the shorter path
  • Speed modes and a hash index so rescans stay fast

File Rules — the folder that keeps itself tidy

Cleanup apps tidy once. File Rules stops the mess coming back. Point it at Downloads, the Desktop, or any folder you choose, and new arrivals get filed the moment they land — sixteen ways to match, nine things to do, including rules that act on whether a file is already a duplicate of something you keep. Folder automation like this is normally an app you buy separately.

Maintain — everyday Mac housekeeping

  • Junk Sweep — caches, logs, and Xcode build junk, sorted by risk
  • Downloads Dust — old files still sitting in Downloads
  • Disk Analysis — which folders are actually using your space
  • Storage Pulse — capacity and free space, including what macOS holds as purgeable
  • Memory Relief — which apps are using the most memory, and quit the ones you choose
  • Stability — crash reports in plain English, with an optional local CPU and memory history

Requirements

  • macOS 13 or later
  • Apple Silicon or Intel

Privacy & safety

Every scan runs on your Mac. Nothing is uploaded, there is no account and no telemetry. Keep a current backup of anything irreplaceable before any cleanup tool touches it — Twinkeep moves files you approve, and quarantines exact duplicates automatically unless you switch that off. See the in-app EULA and Disclaimer.

Native SwiftUI · CryptoKit hashing · App sandbox with user-selected folders
pitch: You know your Mac is full of copies — the same shot, the same MP3 — but you’re not 100% sure what’s safe to remove. Twinkeep finds them, keeps one twin, and quarantines the rest so you can restore anything you still need, or trash it for good when you’re sure.

name: PrecisDesk
shortDescription: Native macOS menu-bar suite for screenshots, screen recording, window layouts, and AirPrint — capture, arrange, and print from one desk.
contentHtml:
What PrecisDesk is

PrecisDesk (PREH-sis-desk) is Precision Solutions’ desktop command center for Mac: screenshots and screen recording, window arrangement, and printing / AirPrint — built natively as a menu-bar utility with in-app editors, history, and hotkeys.

One coherent app for the work you do at the desk every day — capture, arrange, and print — without stitching together separate tools.

Who it’s for

Mac power users, founders, and teams who live in screenshots, demos, multi-monitor layouts, and “print this to my iPhone over Wi‑Fi.”

Capture — screenshots

  • Capture area, window, or fullscreen
  • Quick Access Overlay after capture — preview, annotate, copy, save, or delete
  • Configurable save folders and filename templates
  • Capture history — filter stills vs video, restore, delete

Image editor

  • Crop, shapes, pencil, text, highlighter, counters / step numbers
  • Spotlight / focus, blur, and pixelate for redaction
  • Backgrounds (solid / gradient), undo / redo
  • On-device OCR (Vision) — copy text from the whole image or a selection
  • Color picker (hex / RGB)
  • Non-destructive .precisdesk projects and PNG export

Screen recording & clip editor

  • Record area, window, or display
  • Pause / resume; export MP4 (H.264) and GIF paths
  • Microphone and system audio options
  • Cursor, click highlights, and keystroke overlays
  • Webcam picture-in-picture and auto-captions / subtitles (Pro)
  • In-app clip editor — trim, split, mute, re-encode, export

Arrange — window management

  • Keyboard snap: halves, thirds, quarters, sixths, maximize, center, fill left / right
  • Next / previous display, restore previous size, smaller / larger
  • Repeat-shortcut size cycles and grid placement (2×2 / 3×3)
  • On-screen snap palette for mouse-driven layouts
  • Drag-to-edge / corner snap zones; Stage Manager gap awareness
  • Classic Mac and Windows-style shortcut presets
  • Throw / stash windows, pin mode, gaps, ignored apps, cascade & tile
  • Saved layouts and per-app window rules
  • URL / deeplink API — e.g. precisdesk://snap/left, precisdesk://palette

Full window management uses Accessibility; some advanced snap and AirPrint features may ship on the direct / Gumroad build if the Mac App Store channel needs limits.

Print — AirPrint & destinations

  • Share Mac printers as AirPrint to iPhone, iPad, and other Macs (Bonjour)
  • Per-printer sharing toggles; discover local and network printers
  • Print to folder (PDF), Dropbox / iCloud / chosen paths, or hand off to an app
  • Print job list with pause / resume / cancel and notifications
  • Print annotated screenshots straight from the editor or overlay
  • Quick presets (photo, document, borderless) and paper / quality options

App shell

  • Always-available menu bar app (optional Dock icon)
  • Settings for General, Capture, Windows, Print, Hotkeys, History, and License
  • Permissions onboarding for Screen Recording, Accessibility, Microphone, Camera, and Local Network
  • First-launch legal gate (EULA, Privacy, Disclaimer)

Requirements

  • macOS 14 or later (planned)
  • Native SwiftUI / AppKit app

Capture. Arrange. Print. — one menu-bar suite for the Mac desk.
